In particular, explain whether or not the speed of convergence can be related to eigeninformation (i.e., eigenvalue location and eigenvector conditioning) of the discretized convection-diffusion operators.

evidence.quote: Explain the convergence acceleration of GMRES after the initial (transient) phase that is observed in some convection-diffusion model problems such as the one in~\cite{LieStr05}. In particular, explain whether or not the speed of convergence can be related to eigeninformation (i.e., eigenvalue location and eigenvector conditioning) of the discretized convection-diffusion operators.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a steady linear convection-diffusion boundary-value problem on a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of the form
$$-
u\,\Delta u + \mathbf{w}\cdot
abla u = f \quad	ext{in }\Omega,\qquad u = g \quad	ext{on }\partial\Omega,$$
where $
u>0$ is a (small) diffusion coefficient and $\mathbf{w}\in\mathbb{R}^d$ is a constant convection field. Discretize this problem on a uniform tensor-product grid using either a streamline upwind Petrov–Galerkin (SUPG) finite element method or a standard upwind/central finite difference method, producing a nonsymmetric linear system
$$A x = b,\qquad A\in\mathbb{R}^{N	imes N}.$$
Apply the GMRES iterative method to $Ax=b$ starting from $x_0=0$, and let $r_k = b - Ax_k$ be the $k$-th residual. In numerical experiments on such systems one observes a two-phase convergence behavior: an initial phase of slow ("transient" or stagnation-like) reduction of $\|r_k\|$, followed by a second phase in which the rate of relative residual reduction markedly accelerates.

Provide a rigorous explanation of this convergence acceleration after the initial transient phase. In particular, decide and justify whether the asymptotic (post-transient) rate of GMRES convergence on such discretized convection-diffusion operators $A$ can be quantitatively predicted from spectral information alone—that is, from the location of the eigenvalues of $A$ together with the conditioning $\kappa(V)$ of the eigenvector matrix $V$ in a diagonalization $A = V\Lambda V^{-1}$—or whether the observed convergence rate is intrinsically governed by additional, non-spectral features of $A$ and the right-hand side $b$ (such as the structure of $b$ relative to invariant subspaces, departure from normality measured by pseudospectra or field of values, or the block/Toeplitz structure inherited from the discretization).

status_evidence.title: GMRES Convergence Analysis for a Convection-Diffusion Model Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Instead of using the eigendecomposition of the system matrix (which is ill conditioned), an orthogonal transformation into a block-diagonal matrix with nonsymmetric tridiagonal Toeplitz blocks is used to explain GMRES convergence, showing how the initial period of slow convergence is related to boundary conditions and why convergence in the second stage accelerates.
status_evidence.claim: For specific model problems, the two-phase behavior has been explained via a non-spectral block-Toeplitz analysis, indicating that eigeninformation alone is not descriptive.

status_evidence.title: How Descriptive are GMRES Convergence Bounds?
status_evidence.snippet: Standard eigenvalue-based GMRES convergence bounds can be very pessimistic when the eigenvector basis is highly ill-conditioned, motivating pseudospectral and field-of-values based analyses.
status_evidence.claim: There is general agreement that for highly nonnormal discretized convection-diffusion operators, eigenvalue/eigenvector conditioning bounds are typically not sharp.

artifact.status_search_result: For specific convection-diffusion model problems the two-phase GMRES behavior has been explained without using eigendecompositions: an orthogonal reduction to block tridiagonal Toeplitz form yields sharp descriptions of both the initial transient and the subsequent acceleration. More generally, eigenvalue-plus-eigenvector-conditioning bounds are widely accepted as descriptively poor for these highly nonnormal operators, and pseudospectra/field-of-values or right-hand-side-dependent analyses are required. A complete, fully general explanation that covers all discretized convection-diffusion operators remains an active topic, so the broader question is best regarded as only partially resolved.
